title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals Exhibit Desk: Exchange Period for Late Exhibits on Reopened Hearings
content:
Exhibits recorded as late on an appeal reopened after dismissal give the reopened setting an exhibit exchange period under Unemployment Insurance Appeals.

**Schedule.** The reopened-setting exhibit exchange days are the two-late-exhibit exchange days when two or more exhibits on the appeal stand recorded as late, the one-late-exhibit exchange days when exactly one does, and zero days when none does. The reopened hearing date found from the reopened-setting clock and the reopened-setting window is moved later by these days before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.

| Exhibits on the appeal recorded as late | Exhibit exchange days |
|---|---|
| two or more | 7 |
| exactly one | 4 |
| none | 0 |

## What is counted

- Every exhibit received on the appeal whose record marks it as late — received after the exhibit deadline — from any party.
- Exhibits that met the deadline are not counted, however many there are.

*Cases (hypothetical):* three exhibits, one of them late — 4 days; two late exhibits from the employer and one late from the claimant — 7 days; five exhibits, all received in time — 0 days.

*Illustration:* with exactly one late exhibit, a reopened hearing date found from the clock and the window of Thursday 23 April 2026 moves 4 days later, to Monday 27 April, before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.
